text.p: Thousands of ethnic Albanians demonstrated in the west Macedonian city of Tetovo on Thursday in protest at the alleged poisoning of Albanian children in local schools, Macedonian radio reported.
The demonstrators demanded the resignation of Macedonian health minister Ilija Filipce and yelled "Down with the government, down with (President) Gligorov".
The leader of the (ethnic Albanian) Party for Democratic Prosperity Abdurahman Atili warned of the potential for violence if the "poisoners" are not caught.
"The authorities should as soon as possible find out who are the poisoners. Otherwise the already dramatic situation could provoke chaos, with unpredictable consequences," he said.
"On the eve of the local elections this case has clear political implications," he said
The director of Tetovo's pediatric hospital, Dr Trajan Stamatovski, said that in the past two weeks around 500 school children had sought treatment for headaches, stomach upsets and limb pains.

He said all the children were ethnic Albanians from several primary schools in nearby villages and it was not yet clear what was causing the illnesses. Most children recovered after several days of vitamin treatment.
Health Minister Filipce visited Tetovo on Wednesday evening and said there were no signs of poisoning.
The Health Ministry backed Filipce's assertion with the results of an analyses by the Vienna Forensic Institute.
Deputy Interior Minister Dime Gjurev told a news conference that despite the lack of any medical confirmation of poisoning the police were continuing an investigation into the case.
A U.N. official in the Macedonian capital Skopje told Reuters the situation in Tetovo was tense but under control.

Tetovo has been the site of increasing tensions between minority ethnic Albanians and Macedonians in the run up to local elections scheduled to take place in at least half of the country's municipalities on November 17.
